extracted.subtask_description: A practical seven-step method and accompanying tips for performing substantive revision (as distinct from copyediting) on fiction or creative-writing manuscripts, focusing on structural, character, pacing, and thematic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core distinction: editing vs revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing corrects errors and refines language. Revision involves fundamental changes to structure, character, plot, pacing, perspective, or thematic foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author frames revision as a deeper operation: "Revision entails a change in the rule of law of a given piece." Use this distinction to decide whether you need surface-level edits or structural reworking; avoid treating revision as merely multiple rounds of copyediting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the work uninterrupted
rubrics_metrics.description: Push through discomfort; read the entire piece without making changes and note strong emotional reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do a full read to experience the piece as a reader would. Instead of line-editing, mark where you have emotional responses (confusion, boredom, excitement) to identify high-impact problem areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an outline of what is actually on the page
rubrics_metrics.description: Map the actual structure on the page (not the imagined structure you intended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce a literal outline of scenes, beats, POV shifts, chapter breaks, etc., so you can see the piece's real architecture and compare it to what you thought you wrote.

rubrics_metrics.name: List desired changes without judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Note what you want to alter without evaluating or filtering those desires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect every impulse to change—even small or unreasonable ones—so you have a comprehensive inventory to work from later rather than policing ideas in the moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map desired changes onto the outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Place your listed changes onto the outline to identify clustering patterns and density areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reveals where changes are concentrated (e.g., a particular chapter or character arc) and helps distinguish isolated fixes from systemic problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify deeper/root issues by grouping changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Group changes under categories such as 'characterization,' 'pacing,' 'structure' to surface underlying problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clustering edits into thematic buckets helps you see root causes rather than treating symptoms; use these categories to guide which kinds of interventions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate hierarchical, specific action items
rubrics_metrics.description: Create prioritized, specific tasks that target the grouped issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn broad diagnoses into concrete, ordered steps—hierarchically organized—so you can tackle the most important structural items first and avoid unfocused tinkering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execute revisions one at a time, allowing organic connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Work through action items sequentially, and allow changes to produce new, organic connections in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid trying to address multiple large changes simultaneously; completing one revision can reveal or create other necessary changes. Maintain flexibility to iterate as new relationships emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tactile/manual techniques after major revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Print and hand-retype chapters after significant revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physically retyping helps internalize changes and often surfaces problems that screen-based edits hide; it acts as an extra pass for clarity and cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read aloud or use voice-to-text to detect confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the manuscript aloud or use voice-to-text to catch confusing or awkward phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing the prose exposes rhythm, cadence, and clarity issues that silent reading can miss; voice-to-text can also reveal where sentences aren't clear enough to be spoken naturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time away for perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Step away from the manuscript for a period to gain a fresh perspective before revising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distance increases objectivity and makes it easier to spot structural and tonal issues that become invisible during prolonged immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish concurrent editing from true revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Be conscious of whether you're performing concurrent editing (line-level fixes) or engaging in true revision (fundamental change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowing which mode you're in prevents wasting effort on surface polishing when the piece needs structural rethinking, and conversely prevents overhauling when only edits are required.
